artifacts.summary: Confirms the actual remaining gap is narrower than the task description assumes: two of five described sub-problems (matcher Priority 3, Priority 2 vs. no-task-references rule) are already resolved by later work, and the real fix is threading roadmap_path into the implementer agent contracts (mirroring planner-agent.md's existing Stage 2.5 pattern) plus a distinct silent-0 signal in /todo's Roadmap section branch.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo, task descriptions authored earlier in the roadmap can go stale relative to later, unrelated task work that reshapes the same files. Before planning from a task description, grep git log for the files named in file_scope to check whether the described gap has already been partially or fully closed by intervening tasks -- e.g. task 5 (roadmap_items producer) described a 'three-priority matcher with an unimplemented third tier' that tasks 910/911/914/969/985/21 had already turned into a fully-implemented four-tier matcher by the time research ran.

planner-agent.md already has a working, minimal pattern for giving a fresh-context subagent read-only access to specs/ROADMAP.md: skill-planner/SKILL.md unconditionally sets "roadmap_path": "specs/ROADMAP.md" in the delegation context JSON, and planner-agent.md's Stage 2.5 reads it if present ('MUST NOT: Modify, write to, or create ROADMAP.md. This is a read-only consultation.'). general-research-agent.md has the equivalent as its own Stage 1.5. Any other agent needing ROADMAP.md awareness (e.g. general-implementation-agent.md, which currently has none) should copy this exact shape rather than inventing a new one.

specs/ROADMAP.md is fully exempt from .claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md because that rule's own scope line excludes all of specs/**. Task-number prose ("task 710", "(Task N)") in ROADMAP.md is not a rule violation and needs no marker -- do not propose reconciliation work between roadmap annotation formats and that rule without first re-checking its scope line.
